claim: EGGLND is the SETTLED-egg handler and its first act is to load the hatch wait into the egg's own PJOYT workspace. This is the general egg wait — RAMDEF.SRC:393 declares EGGWT as 'TIME TO WAIT BEFORE STARTING EGG HATCHIN SEQUENCE' — and every egg that LANDS reaches it, whatever killed it.

source.verbatim: EGGLND	LDA	EGGWT		GET CURRENT WAIT TIME

claim: The wait is stored in the egg's PJOYT, the same per-process timer slot the enemy brains use for their own countdowns.

THE UNIT OF THE WAIT. The settled-egg loop costs a PCNAP 12 per pass, and the pass is what spends one tick of the wait — so a wait of n is n*12 DISPLAY FRAMES, not n frames. The nap sits between EGGLND's load (:3224) and the DEC PJOYT,U at :3236, and the BNE at :3237 closes the loop back above it, so the nap is paid once per decrement rather than once in total. Reading EGGWT as a frame count runs every egg hatch twelve times too fast.
The wait counts DOWN one per loop pass, and the loop repeats until it reaches zero. EGGLN2 (:3226) is the head this branches back to.
The wait loop's closing branch. Non-zero PJOYT re-enters EGGLN2 and pays another PCNAP 12; only a zero falls through to the hatch.

EGGWT2 is a SEPARATE row from EGGWT and a separate wait: it is read once during EGG-WAVE setup, and RAMDEF.SRC:395 declares it 'TIME TO WAIT BEFORE STARTING EGG HATCHIN (EGG WAVES)'. So an egg-wave egg enters holding EGGWT2 while an egg that lands takes EGGWT. At GA1 5 the two differ from wave 1 onward (56 vs 64), so wiring one row to both paths is observable, not cosmetic.

source.verbatim: LDB	EGGWT2		INITIAL EGG WAITING TIME

claim: DEATH3 TRANSFERS the dying enemy's remaining egg count to the egg it leaves rather than inventing a fresh complement. The count lives on the BIRD (PEGG), and this is the first half of the cycle that walks it down toward permadeath.

source.verbatim: LDA	PEGG,U		TRANSFER NBR OF EGG LEFT

claim: The transferred count is then decremented — the egg costs the enemy one of its four. The BNE at :3002 branches away while the result is non-zero ('BR=YOU CAN GET MORE EGGS'), so only the decrement that REACHES ZERO falls through to the scoring block below.

source.verbatim: DEC	PEGG,Y		YOU CAN ONLY SQUEEZE SO MUCH BLOOD FROM AN EGG

claim: THE VICTOR GUARD. Before scoring the last egg the ROM loads the victor's workspace and skips the award entirely when it is zero — a death with no victor (the lava troll's) earns nobody anything. The BEQ target 1$ is the routine's own epilogue at :3007, the same label the eggs-remaining BNE at :3002 takes.

source.verbatim: LDU	,S		GET VICTORS WORKSPACE (CURRENTLY DIEING ENEMY)

claim: EGGSCR's SECOND call site, and the one this port did not model. An enemy's LAST egg is scored to the victor at the moment of the kill, with no catch required — distinct from the PLYEGG catch site at :3021 that jt8-4 wired. grep 'JSR EGGSCR' over JOUSTRV4.SRC returns exactly these two.

The hatch hands the egg count BACK to the buzzard that remounts. This is the half that makes permadeath reachable at all: without it every remounted bird forgets its count, the four-egg complement is effectively infinite, and the DEATH3 award at :3006 can never fire in play.

source.verbatim: LDA	PEGG,U		MAINTAIN NBR OF EGGS LEFT IN THE BIRD

claim: PWHCH is a one-byte per-player workspace cell, declared with Williams's own name for the mechanic: a PRE-MATURE HATCHING EGG. Its 'IF >0' agrees exactly with the rule CREGG implements, PROVIDED '>0' is read as the SIGNED comparison the BMI at :2889 performs: v > 0 is true precisely when v-1 is non-negative, which holds for every value the counter reaches (2, 1, 0, $FF, $FE and down). Enumerated over all 256 byte values, the only signed disagreement is $80, which a counter that only decrements from 2 can never hold. Read UNSIGNED the two part company from $81 up — including the $FF the third egg lands on — so the reading is load-bearing even though the comment is not loose. This claim replaces an earlier version that called the declaration looser than the code and offered 'a cell holding 1 still buys a shortening' as evidence; a cell holding 1 IS >0, so that example showed agreement.

source.verbatim: PWHCH	RMB	1	IF >0 A PRE-MATURE HATCHING EGG TO BE CREATED

claim: CREGG's egg-creation block loads the wave's hatch time from PEGGTM — the EGGWT2-derived per-wave wait set at egg-wave setup (:2767). This is the value the pre-mature shortening subtracts FROM, and it is still in the B accumulator when the MUL at :2891 runs, which is what makes the cut a fraction of the wave's own wait rather than a fixed number of frames.

The wait is stored into the new egg's PJOYT, the per-process timer the settled-egg loop (EGGLND, :3224-3237) counts down. Every egg CREGG creates starts here; only the first two then have this value reduced.

The pre-mature counter is decremented once per egg CREGG creates. Together with the BMI on the next line this is what decides HOW MANY eggs of the twelve are shortened: DEC sets N from bit 7 of the RESULT, so starting from the 2 loaded at :2776 the decrement to 1 and the decrement to 0 both fall through, and the decrement to $FF is the first to branch away. TWO eggs, matching the :2776 comment — not three.

source.verbatim: DEC	PWHCH,U		ANYMORE EGGS TO HATCH PREMATURLY?

claim: The branch that skips the shortening. BMI is taken only when the decremented PWHCH has gone NEGATIVE, and its target 20$ (:2895) is the line immediately after the shortening block, so a skip leaves the egg holding the full PEGGTM wait it was given at :2887.

The draw. VRAND yields a random number in 0-127 — a range this comment states and two other sites depend on: :2795 has to ROLA a draw to 'GET RANDOM NBR 0 TO 255', and the ledge select at :2782-2784 multiplies a draw by 6*2 to index the six-entry EGLEDG table, which a 0-255 draw would overrun.

The 6809 MUL multiplies A (the 0-127 draw) by B (the wave's hatch time, still held from :2886) and leaves the 16-bit product in D, high byte in A. Taking only that high byte is a divide by 256, so with the draw capped at 127 the result can never reach half the wait — which is exactly what Williams's comment claims. A pre-mature egg is EARLY, never instant.

source.verbatim: MUL			GET A RANDOM TIME 1/2 OF THE RANGE

claim: The high byte of the product is negated, so the ADDA on the next line SUBTRACTS it.
The negated cut is added to the egg's stored hatch time, giving wait minus (draw * wait / 256).

The shortened value is written back over the egg's PJOYT. This is the whole effect of PWHCH: two of an egg wave's twelve eggs hatch sooner than the other ten, by an amount drawn per egg, so the wave's twelve maturities no longer land on one frame.
